p: elders which are among you: He describes peculiarly the office of the Elders, that is to say, of them that have the care of the Church.

I exhort: He uses a preface concerning the circumstance of his own person: that is, that he as their companion communes with them not of manners which he knows not, but in which he is as well experienced as any, and propounds to them no other condition but that which he himself has sustained before them, and still takes the same trouble, and also has the same hope together with them.
The first rule: he that is a shepherd let him feed the flock.
flock of God which is: The second: Let not shepherd consider, that the flock is not his, but Gods.
among you: The third: Let not shepherds invade other men's flocks, but let them feed that which God hath committed unto them.

taking the oversight thereof: Let the shepherds govern the Church with the word and example of godly and unblamable life, not by force but willingly, not for greedy gain, but with a ready mind, not as lords over God's portion and heritage, but as his ministers.
heritage: Which is the Christian people.

And when the chief Shepherd shall: That the shepherds' minds are not overcome either with the wickedness of men, or their cruelty, he warns them to continually look at the chief shepherd, and the crown which is laid up for them in heaven.
Likewise: He commends many peculiar Christian virtues, and especially modesty: an admonition all of us need, but especially the younger ones by reason of the perverseness and pride of that age.

for God resisteth the proud: Because pride seems to many to be the way to the glory of this life, the apostle testifies to the opposite, that dishonour and shame is the reward of pride, and glory the reward of modesty.

under the mighty hand of God: Because those proud and lofty spirits threaten the modest and humble, the apostle warns us to set the power of God against the vanity of proud men, and to rely completely on his providence.
Be sober: The cruelty of Satan, who seeks by all means to devour us, is overcome by watchfulness and faith.

knowing that the same afflictions are: The persecutions which Satan stirs up, are neither new nor proper to any one man, but from old and ancient times common to the whole Church, and therefore we must suffer patiently, in which we have such and so many fellows of our conflicts and combats.
brethren that are in the world: Amongst your brethren which are dispersed throughout the world.

But the God of all grace: He seals up as with a seal the former exhortation with a solemn prayer, again willing them to ask increase of strength at his hands, of whom they had the beginning, and hope to have the accomplishment: that is, of God the Father in Christ Jesus, in whom we are sure of the glory of eternal life.

By Silvanus: Continuance and perseverance in the doctrine of the apostles is the only ground and foundation of Christian strength: Now the sum of the apostles doctrine, is salvation freely given by God.
The church that is at: Familiar salutations.
Babylon: In that famous city of Assyria, where Peter the apostle of circumcision then was.
